- **Title**: feat(1079): SDK slice 4 — HostExtensionApi: declared builder-gated extensions (E6/E7/E8)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1079-sdk-host-slice4` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +653
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T17:27:38Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T17:40:13Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

## Delivered vs remaining slices

| Slice | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — profiles + builder foundation | ✅ #1091 |
| 2 — live wiring (`wireAgentCore`); CLI converts | ✅ #1230 |
| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. Verification here is static 1:1: every referenced symbol/field checked against source (`CapabilityState` hierarchy, `builtInProfiles`, `TaskToolConfig.childTools`, `CapabilityPlanEntry`, exception contracts), no `hostTools` callers remain, fixture and imports migrated. **CI is the real gate** — analyze + the extended `test/hosts/` matrix (new `host_extension_api_test.dart`: E6 construction rejections, E7 collision naming, E8 hiding/reason surfacing, AC9 core-identity and child-pool pins) run there.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

Now I have a good understanding of the wiring. Key observations so far:

1. `_wireExtensions` uses `profile.name` — the ORIGINAL profile, not the run-narrowed one (`runProfile`). The doc comment says "run-narrowing renames the profile (`cli.run`) but an extension's matrix is declared per base profile". So when `_narrowToServices` creates a narrowed profile, the name is `cli.run` — but `_wireExtensions` receives `profile.name` (the base profile passed in, e.g. `cli`). Good — consistent with the comment. But wait — what if the caller passes a profile that was ALREADY narrowed (e.g. constructed via `narrowed()` with name `cli.narrowed`)? Then the extension state lookup uses `cli.narrowed` which wouldn't match `cli`. That's the documented behavior though (declare per base profile). Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: `narrowed()` without a name gives `cli.narrowed`. The comment only addresses run-narrowing. This might be an edge but it's documented.

2. **Potential issue — hidden extensions and the E7 check.** `_rejectToolIdCollisions` only includes extension groups `where((w) => !w.isHidden)`. Good — off extensions contribute no tools.

3. **Potential issue — duplicate tool ids WITHIN the SDK core or task surface.** The E7 check covers core vs task vs extensions. Within one extension duplicates are rejected at construction. - **Branch**: `feat/1079-sdk-host-slice4` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +653
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-07T17:27:38Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T17:40:13Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

## Delivered vs remaining slices

| Slice | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — profiles + builder foundation | ✅ #1091 |
| 2 — live wiring (`wireAgentCore`); CLI converts | ✅ #1230 |
| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. Verification here is static 1:1: every referenced symbol/field checked against source (`CapabilityState` hierarchy, `builtInProfiles`, `TaskToolConfig.childTools`, `CapabilityPlanEntry`, exception contracts), no `hostTools` callers remain, fixture and imports migrated. **CI is the real gate** — analyze + the extended `test/hosts/` matrix (new `host_extension_api_test.dart`: E6 construction rejections, E7 collision naming, E8 hiding/reason surfacing, AC9 core-identity and child-pool pins) run there.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

## PR Description

Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe

  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`

Now I have a good understanding of the wiring. Key observations so far:

1. `_wireExtensions` uses `profile.name` — the ORIGINAL profile, not the run-narrowed one (`runProfile`). The doc comment says "run-narrowing renames the profile (`cli.run`) but an extension's matrix is declared per base profile". So when `_narrowToServices` creates a narrowed profile, the name is `cli.run` — but `_wireExtensions` receives `profile.name` (the base profile passed in, e.g. `cli`). Good — consistent with the comment. But wait — what if the caller passes a profile that was ALREADY narrowed (e.g. constructed via `narrowed()` with name `cli.narrowed`)? Then the extension state lookup uses `cli.narrowed` which wouldn't match `cli`. That's the documented behavior though (declare per base profile). Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: `narrowed()` without a name gives `cli.narrowed`. The comment only addresses run-narrowing. This might be an edge but it's documented.

2. **Potential issue — hidden extensions and the E7 check.** `_rejectToolIdCollisions` only includes extension groups `where((w) => !w.isHidden)`. Good — off extensions contribute no tools.

3. **Potential issue — duplicate tool ids WITHIN the SDK core or task surface.** The E7 check covers core vs task vs extensions. Within one extension duplicates are rejected at construction. Within the SDK core itself — if `_buildCoreTools` produced a duplicate (a bug), the E7 check would catch it as a collision within 'the SDK core' since `owner` map is shared. Actually yes — the claim loop would catch it because all tools go into the same `owner` map. Fine.

4. **Ordering issue**: extension tools are appended to `tools` BEFORE the task complex assembles, and the task complex uses `coreTools: tools` as `childTools`. So children get extension tools. And the E7 check runs after. Fine.

5. **The E7 check happens AFTER `wireAgentCore` builds the task complex but before registry assembly.** The `WiredAgentCore._` constructor is called after the check, so a throw prevents the core from being constructed. OK.

6. **Hidden extensions still appear in `WiredAgentCore.extensions`** with empty tools and hiddenReason. That's per spec (E8).

Now let me check the E8 doc claim: "`WiredHostExtension`... the tools that reached the stack, or the off reason". And `hiddenReason`: "the profile's declared off reason, never empty". Construction validates blank reasons for off states — yes, `HostExtension` constructor rejects blank reasons. OK.

7. **`WiredHostExtension` constructor with `List.unmodifiable`** — `_wireExtensions` passes `tools: const []` for hidden and `tools: List.unmodifiable(extension.tools)` for on. The `WiredHostExtension` constructor is `const` but called non-const here. Fine.

8. **The `CapabilityOffState` in `_wireExtensions` switch**: `final CapabilityOffState off => ...` then `_ => ...` catches `CapabilityOnState`. But what about `CapabilityTransportState`? The constructor rejects transport states... wait, does it? The constructor loop: `if (entry.value is CapabilityTransportState) throw`. Yes — transport states rejected at construction. So at wire time only On/Off remain. The `_` arm handles `CapabilityOnState`. OK.

But hold on — the constructor validates `profileStates` entries at construction, rejecting transport states for ANY key. Good.

9. **`stateFor` on a custom profile**: If a host wires a custom profile named e.g. `yoclip-host`, and the extension doesn't declare `yoclip-host`, `stateFor` returns null → `HostWiringException` (wire-time E6). This is tested.

## PR Description

Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

## Delivered vs remaining slices

| Slice | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — profiles + builder foundation | ✅ #1091 |
| 2 — live wiring (`wireAgentCore`); CLI converts | ✅ #1230 |
| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T17:40:13Z

## PR Description

Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

## Delivered vs remaining slices

| Slice | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — profiles + builder foundation | ✅ #1091 |
| 2 — live wiring (`wireAgentCore`); CLI converts | ✅ #1230 |
| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. Verification here is static 1:1: every referenced symbol/field checked against source (`CapabilityState` hierarchy, `builtInProfiles`, `TaskToolConfig.childTools`, `CapabilityPlanEntry`, exception contracts), no `hostTools` callers remain, fixture and imports migrated. **CI is the real gate** — analyze + the extended `test/hosts/` matrix (new `host_extension_api_test.dart`: E6 construction rejections, E7 collision naming, E8 hiding/reason surfacing, AC9 core-identity and child-pool pins) run there.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"ios"')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a transport state is rejected — tool extensions have no '
+        'transport dimension', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {
+            ..._states(),
+            'cli': const CapabilityTransportState({'file'}, 'why not'),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an off state without a reason is rejected (off is never '
+        'silent)', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {..._states(), 'cli': const CapabilityOffState(' ')},
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a duplicate tool id inside one extension is rejected', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut'), _tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>().having(
+            (e) => e.message,
+            'message',
+            contains('yoclip_cut'),
+          ),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('every built-in profile declared constructs', () {
+      expect(

    "description": "Part of #1079 (epic slice — remaining slices stay on the GOAL; no Closes).

## What landed (slice 4 — issue component 4, `HostExtensionApi`)

Host extensions become **declared, builder-gated surface** instead of a raw tool list:

- **New** `lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart` — `HostExtension` (named registrant: tools + explicit state for **every built-in profile at birth**, E6 — no implicit default; a transport state or blank off-reason is rejected; custom-profile states validate at wire time) and `WiredHostExtension` (per-extension outcome: wired tools, or the off reason, E8).
- **Builder gating** in `wireAgentCore` (`host_agent_wiring.dart`): extension tools splice after the SDK core in the canonical tail position; **E7** — tool-id collisions across the SDK core / gated task surface / extensions throw `HostWiringException` at build time naming both registrants. The loud check lives in the builder, not `ToolRegistry` (whose replace-and-note leniency stays for the child-pool contract, #862, and the per-run `buildAgentStack(additionalTools:)` surface).
- **E8**: a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason on the new `WiredAgentCore.extensions` field — the hide-if-off invariant, extension edition.
- **Additive-only (AC9/UT-5)**: the extension surface carries tools + declarations, nothing else; the only route to "replace" a core tool is a colliding id and E7 slams it (pinned by test). Core tools, env chain and per-capability plan are byte-identical with and without an extension (pinned by test), and extension tools ride the child tool pool like the core surface.
- **CLI migration**: `AgentCli` passes its plugin tools as a declared `cli-plugins` extension — `on` for the CLI profile, `off(reason)` for the other six (a host adopting another profile declares its own extensions). Registry order is unchanged.
- **AGENTS.md**: capability rules extended with the extension contract (E6/E7/E8 + additive-only), per AC8.

## Delivered vs remaining slices

| Slice | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — profiles + builder foundation | ✅ #1091 |
| 2 — live wiring (`wireAgentCore`); CLI converts | ✅ #1230 |
| 3 — builder-owned task/subagent/fabric complex | ✅ #1313 |
| 4 — HostExtensionApi: E6 matrix at birth, E7 build-time collisions, E8 hiding, AC9 additive-only pin | **this PR** |
| 5 — flutter_app adopts the builder (AC1 second half: app hand-wiring deleted to profile + platform services) | remaining |
| 6 — IT-5 record-level byte parity (JSONL kinds/compaction/memory record diff for a registered extension host, the YoClip scenario end-to-end) | remaining |
| 7 — extension prompt-sections/bridges registration; #1077/#1078 suites rewired through the builder (AC5) | remaining |

## Local gate disclosure (honest)

Local `dart` is the Flutter-cask wrapper (its engine-stamp updater can't write the shared cache), and the raw dart-sdk run was **SIGKILLed by the host guard (exit 137) on the first attempt** — per lane policy I did not retry. Verification here is static 1:1: every referenced symbol/field checked against source (`CapabilityState` hierarchy, `builtInProfiles`, `TaskToolConfig.childTools`, `CapabilityPlanEntry`, exception contracts), no `hostTools` callers remain, fixture and imports migrated. **CI is the real gate** — analyze + the extended `test/hosts/` matrix (new `host_extension_api_test.dart`: E6 construction rejections, E7 collision naming, E8 hiding/reason surfacing, AC9 core-identity and child-pool pins) run there."
  }

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"ios"')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a transport state is rejected — tool extensions have no '
+        'transport dimension', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {
+            ..._states(),
+            'cli': const CapabilityTransportState({'file'}, 'why not'),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an off state without a reason is rejected (off is never '
+        'silent)', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {..._states(), 'cli': const CapabilityOffState(' ')},
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a duplicate tool id inside one extension is rejected', () {
+      expect(

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"ios"')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a transport state is rejected — tool extensions have no '
+        'transport dimension', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {
+            ..._states(),
+            'cli': const CapabilityTransportState({'file'}, 'why not'),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an off state without a reason is rejected (off is never '
+        'silent)', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {..._states(), 'cli': const CapabilityOffState(' ')},
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a duplicate tool id inside one extension is rejected', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut'), _tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>().having(
+            (e) => e.message,
+            'message',
+            contains('yoclip_cut'),
+          ),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('every built-in profile declared constructs', () {
+      expect(
+        HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        isA<HostExtension>(),

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"ios"')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a transport state is rejected — tool extensions have no '
+        'transport dimension', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {
+            ..._states(),
+            'cli': const CapabilityTransportState({'file'}, 'why not'),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an off state without a reason is rejected (off is never '
+        'silent)', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {..._states(), 'cli': const CapabilityOffState(' ')},
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a duplicate tool id inside one extension is rejected', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut'), _tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>().having(
+            (e) => e.message,
+            'message',
+            contains('yoclip_cut'),
+          ),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('every built-in profile declared constructs', () {
+      expect(
+        HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        isA<HostExtension>(),
+      );
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('E7 — collisions rejected at build time', () {
+    test('an extension id colliding with the SDK core throws naming both '
+        'registrants (the negative-API pin: there is NO override point '
+        'for a core tool)', () {
+      final services = AgentCoreServices(
+        baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
+        extensions: [
+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yoclip',
+            tools: [_tool('read')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+        ],
+      );
+      expect(
+        () => wireAgentCore(profile: cliProfile, services: services),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostWiringException>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"read"'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('the SDK core'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('two extensions colliding with each other throw naming both', () {
+      final services = AgentCoreServices(
+        baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),

+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yoclip',
+            tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+          HostExtension(

+

+        () {
+      final wired = wireAgentCore(
+        profile: cliProfile,
+        services: AgentCoreServices(

      # fixture-self-tested (breach fails + files the body; fit passes;
      # warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
