      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time

      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN

+/// hiding with the reason surfaced, and the additive-only core
+/// invariance contract (AC9/UT-5 — the only route to "replace" a core
+/// tool is a colliding id, and E7 slams it).
+library;
+
+import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart';
+import 'package:test/test.dart';
+
+AgentTool _tool(String name) => AgentTool(
+  name: name,
+  label: name,
+  description: 'test',
+  parameters: {},
+  execute: (arguments, cancelToken, onUpdate) async =>
+      ToolExecutionResult.text('ok'),
+);
+
+/// All seven built-in profiles `on`; [offOn] (when given) `off` with a
+/// reason instead.
+Map<String, CapabilityState> _states({String? offOn}) => {
+  for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+    profile: profile == offOn
+        ? const CapabilityOffState('not on this host')
+        : const CapabilityOnState(),
+};
+
+final _model = Model(
+  id: 'test-model',
+  api: 'openai-completions',
+  provider: 'test',
+  baseUrl: 'http://localhost',
+  contextWindow: 8192,
+  maxTokens: 1024,
+);
+
+AssistantMessageEventStream _fakeStream(
+  Model model,
+  Context context, {
+  CancelToken? cancelToken,
+}) => AssistantMessageEventStream();
+
+void main() {
+  group('E6 — extension matrix declared at birth', () {
+    test('a missing built-in profile is rejected, extension and profile '
+        'named', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: {
+            for (final profile in builtInProfiles.keys)
+              if (profile != 'ios') profile: const CapabilityOnState(),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"ios"')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a transport state is rejected — tool extensions have no '
+        'transport dimension', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {
+            ..._states(),
+            'cli': const CapabilityTransportState({'file'}, 'why not'),
+          },
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an off state without a reason is rejected (off is never '
+        'silent)', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          profileStates: {..._states(), 'cli': const CapabilityOffState(' ')},
+        ),
+        throwsA(isA<HostProfileViolation>()),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('a duplicate tool id inside one extension is rejected', () {
+      expect(
+        () => HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut'), _tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostProfileViolation>().having(
+            (e) => e.message,
+            'message',
+            contains('yoclip_cut'),
+          ),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('every built-in profile declared constructs', () {
+      expect(
+        HostExtension(
+          name: 'yoclip',
+          tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+          profileStates: _states(),
+        ),
+        isA<HostExtension>(),
+      );
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('E7 — collisions rejected at build time', () {
+    test('an extension id colliding with the SDK core throws naming both '
+        'registrants (the negative-API pin: there is NO override point '
+        'for a core tool)', () {
+      final services = AgentCoreServices(
+        baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
+        extensions: [
+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yoclip',
+            tools: [_tool('read')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+        ],
+      );
+      expect(
+        () => wireAgentCore(profile: cliProfile, services: services),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostWiringException>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('"read"'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('the SDK core'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('two extensions colliding with each other throw naming both', () {
+      final services = AgentCoreServices(
+        baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
+        extensions: [
+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yoclip',
+            tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yotrim',
+            tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+        ],
+      );
+      expect(
+        () => wireAgentCore(profile: cliProfile, services: services),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostWiringException>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yotrim')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+
+    test('an extension id colliding with the gated task surface throws '
+        'naming both', () {
+      final services = _subagentServices(
+        extensions: [
+          HostExtension(
+            name: 'yoclip',
+            tools: [_tool('task_status')],
+            profileStates: _states(),
+          ),
+        ],
+      );
+      expect(
+        () => wireAgentCore(profile: cliProfile, services: services),
+        throwsA(
+          isA<HostWiringException>()
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('task_status'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('task surface'))
+              .having((e) => e.message, 'message', contains('yoclip')),
+        ),
+      );
+    });
+  });
+
+  group('E8 — off means hidden with a surfaced reason', () {
+    test('a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its '
+        'reason', () {
+      final wired = wireAgentCore(
+        profile: cliProfile,
+        services: AgentCoreServices(
+          baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
+          extensions: [
+            HostExtension(
+              name: 'yoclip',
+              tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+              profileStates: _states(offOn: cliProfile.name),
+            ),
+          ],
+        ),
+      );
+      expect(wired.tools.map((t) => t.name), isNot(contains('yoclip_cut')));
+      expect(wired.extensions, hasLength(1));
+      final outcome = wired.extensions.single;
+      expect(outcome.extension.name, 'yoclip');
+      expect(outcome.isHidden, isTrue);
+      expect(outcome.hiddenReason, 'not on this host');
+      expect(outcome.tools, isEmpty);
+    });
+
+    test('an on extension wires its tools in the canonical tail position',
+        () {
+      final wired = wireAgentCore(
+        profile: cliProfile,
+        services: AgentCoreServices(
+          baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
+          extensions: [
+            HostExtension(
+              name: 'yoclip',
+              tools: [_tool('yoclip_cut')],
+              profileStates: _states(),
+            ),
+          ],
+        ),
+      );

name: flutter_agent_harness
description: >-
  Cross-platform AI agent harness for Dart and Flutter: streaming provider
  adapters, agent loop with tools, session persistence, context compaction.
version: 1.0.526
# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

Now I have a good understanding of the wiring. Key observations so far:

1. `_wireExtensions` uses `profile.name` — the ORIGINAL profile, not the run-narrowed one (`runProfile`). The doc comment says "run-narrowing renames the profile (`cli.run`) but an extension's matrix is declared per base profile". So when `_narrowToServices` creates a narrowed profile, the name is `cli.run` — but `_wireExtensions` receives `profile.name` (the base profile passed in, e.g. `cli`). Good — consistent with the comment. But wait — what if the caller passes a profile that was ALREADY narrowed (e.g. constructed via `narrowed()` with name `cli.narrowed`)? Then the extension state lookup uses `cli.narrowed` which wouldn't match `cli`. That's the documented behavior though (declare per base profile). Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: `narrowed()` without a name gives `cli.narrowed`. The comment only addresses run-narrowing. This might be an edge but it's documented.

2. **Potential issue — hidden extensions and the E7 check.** `_rejectToolIdCollisions` only includes extension groups `where((w) => !w.isHidden)`. Good — off extensions contribute no tools.

3. **Potential issue — duplicate tool ids WITHIN the SDK core or task surface.** The E7 check covers core vs task vs extensions. Within one extension duplicates are rejected at construction.   code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.

  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate

  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay

  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.

  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

Now I have a good understanding of the wiring. Key observations so far:

1. `_wireExtensions` uses `profile.name` — the ORIGINAL profile, not the run-narrowed one (`runProfile`). The doc comment says "run-narrowing renames the profile (`cli.run`) but an extension's matrix is declared per base profile". So when `_narrowToServices` creates a narrowed profile, the name is `cli.run` — but `_wireExtensions` receives `profile.name` (the base profile passed in, e.g. `cli`). Good — consistent with the comment. But wait — what if the caller passes a profile that was ALREADY narrowed (e.g. constructed via `narrowed()` with name `cli.narrowed`)? Then the extension state lookup uses `cli.narrowed` which wouldn't match `cli`. That's the documented behavior though (declare per base profile). Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: `narrowed()` without a name gives `cli.narrowed`. The comment only addresses run-narrowing. This might be an edge but it's documented.

2. **Potential issue — hidden extensions and the E7 check.** `_rejectToolIdCollisions` only includes extension groups `where((w) => !w.isHidden)`. Good — off extensions contribute no tools.

3. **Potential issue — duplicate tool ids WITHIN the SDK core or task surface.** The E7 check covers core vs task vs extensions. Within one extension duplicates are rejected at construction. Within the SDK core itself — if `_buildCoreTools` produced a duplicate (a bug), the E7 check would catch it as a collision within 'the SDK core' since `owner` map is shared. Actually yes — the claim loop would catch it because all tools go into the same `owner` map. Fine.

4. **Ordering issue**: extension tools are appended to `tools` BEFORE the task complex assembles, and the task complex uses `coreTools: tools` as `childTools`. So children get extension tools. And the E7 check runs after. Fine.

5. **The E7 check happens AFTER `wireAgentCore` builds the task complex but before registry assembly.** The `WiredAgentCore._` constructor is called after the check, so a throw prevents the core from being constructed. OK.

6. **Hidden extensions still appear in `WiredAgentCore.extensions`** with empty tools and hiddenReason. That's per spec (E8).

Now let me check the E8 doc claim: "`WiredHostExtension`... the tools that reached the stack, or the off reason". And `hiddenReason`: "the profile's declared off reason, never empty". Construction validates blank reasons for off states — yes, `HostExtension` constructor rejects blank reasons. OK.

7. **`WiredHostExtension` constructor with `List.unmodifiable`** — `_wireExtensions` passes `tools: const []` for hidden and `tools: List.unmodifiable(extension.tools)` for on. The `WiredHostExtension` constructor is `const` but called non-const here. Fine.

8. **The `CapabilityOffState` in `_wireExtensions` switch**: `final CapabilityOffState off => ...` then `_ => ...` catches `CapabilityOnState`. But what about `CapabilityTransportState`? The constructor rejects transport states... wait, does it? The constructor loop: `if (entry.value is CapabilityTransportState) throw`. Yes — transport states rejected at construction. So at wire time only On/Off remain. The `_` arm handles `CapabilityOnState`. OK.

But hold on — the constructor validates `profileStates` entries at construction, rejecting transport states for ANY key. Good.

9. **`stateFor` on a custom profile**: If a host wires a custom profile named e.g. `yoclip-host`, and the extension doesn't declare `yoclip-host`, `stateFor` returns null → `HostWiringException` (wire-time E6). This is tested.

10. Now a subtle one: `_wireExtensions` is called with `profileName: profile.name` where `profile` is the parameter passed to `wireAgentCore` — NOT `runProfile` (the narrowed one). Consider: the extension declares state for `cli` = on. The host passes `cliProfile`. Run-narrowing happens on capabilities, not extensions — an extension tool wires regardless of whether its host capability... wait, actually there's no gating of extensions against `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`! Interesting: the profile has a `hostExtensionApi` capability (all seven built-ins have it `on`). If a custom profile declares `hostExtensionApi` OFF, should extensions still wire? Let me check: `wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally. The plan gates the other capabilities but extensions are NOT gated on `plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability`. Hmm. Is that an issue?

Looking at the catalog: `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi: (all: {}, defaults: {})` — no required services. All seven built-in profiles declare it `on`. A custom profile could declare it `off` (e.g. "embed floor: no extension tools"). With this PR, the extension would STILL wire because `_wireExtensions` never consults the plan. That's a real gap: the capability row `hostExtensionApi` exists in the matrix and is declared on/off per profile, but the builder ignores it when wiring extensions. The E6/E8 matrix drives purely on the extension's own `profileStates`, not the profile's `hostExtensionApi` capability state.

Is this in-scope for slice 4? The issue component 4 is HostExtensionApi. The capability row exists since slice 1. Arguably the gating should be: if profile's `hostExtensionApi` is off, extensions don't wire (maybe all hidden with that reason). Let me check if any built-in profile has it off — no, all seven are `on`. So with built-in profiles there's no behavioral difference. For custom profiles: a host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` would expect extensions to hide, but they'd wire anyway. This is a legitimate correctness/consistency finding — the capability matrix declares a cell that has no effect. # Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign

  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /

  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.

  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an

Now I have a good understanding of the wiring. Key observations so far:

1. `_wireExtensions` uses `profile.name` — the ORIGINAL profile, not the run-narrowed one (`runProfile`). The doc comment says "run-narrowing renames the profile (`cli.run`) but an extension's matrix is declared per base profile". So when `_narrowToServices` creates a narrowed profile, the name is `cli.run` — but `_wireExtensions` receives `profile.name` (the base profile passed in, e.g. `cli`). Good — consistent with the comment. But wait — what if the caller passes a profile that was ALREADY narrowed (e.g. constructed via `narrowed()` with name `cli.narrowed`)? Then the extension state lookup uses `cli.narrowed` which wouldn't match `cli`. That's the documented behavior though (declare per base profile). Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: `narrowed()` without a name gives `cli.narrowed`. The comment only addresses run-narrowing. This might be an edge but it's documented.

2. **Potential issue — hidden extensions and the E7 check.** `_rejectToolIdCollisions` only includes extension groups `where((w) => !w.isHidden)`. Good — off extensions contribute no tools.

3. **Potential issue — duplicate tool ids WITHIN the SDK core or task surface.** The E7 check covers core vs task vs extensions. Within one extension duplicates are rejected at construction. Within the SDK core itself — if `_buildCoreTools` produced a duplicate (a bug), the E7 check would catch it as a collision within 'the SDK core' since `owner` map is shared. Actually yes — the claim loop would catch it because all tools go into the same `owner` map. Fine.

4. **Ordering issue**: extension tools are appended to `tools` BEFORE the task complex assembles, and the task complex uses `coreTools: tools` as `childTools`. So children get extension tools. And the E7 check runs after. Fine.

5. **The E7 check happens AFTER `wireAgentCore` builds the task complex but before registry assembly.** The `WiredAgentCore._` constructor is called after the check, so a throw prevents the core from being constructed. OK.

6. **Hidden extensions still appear in `WiredAgentCore.extensions`** with empty tools and hiddenReason. That's per spec (E8).

Now let me check the E8 doc claim: "`WiredHostExtension`... the tools that reached the stack, or the off reason". And `hiddenReason`: "the profile's declared off reason, never empty". Construction validates blank reasons for off states — yes, `HostExtension` constructor rejects blank reasons. OK.

7. **`WiredHostExtension` constructor with `List.unmodifiable`** — `_wireExtensions` passes `tools: const []` for hidden and `tools: List.unmodifiable(extension.tools)` for on. The `WiredHostExtension` constructor is `const` but called non-const here. Fine.

8. **The `CapabilityOffState` in `_wireExtensions` switch**: `final CapabilityOffState off => ...` then `_ => ...` catches `CapabilityOnState`. But what about `CapabilityTransportState`? The constructor rejects transport states... wait, does it? The constructor loop: `if (entry.value is CapabilityTransportState) throw`. Yes — transport states rejected at construction. So at wire time only On/Off remain. The `_` arm handles `CapabilityOnState`. OK.

But hold on — the constructor validates `profileStates` entries at construction, rejecting transport states for ANY key. Good.

9. **`stateFor` on a custom profile**: If a host wires a custom profile named e.g. `yoclip-host`, and the extension doesn't declare `yoclip-host`, `stateFor` returns null → `HostWiringException` (wire-time E6). This is tested.

10. Now a subtle one: `_wireExtensions` is called with `profileName: profile.name` where `profile` is the parameter passed to `wireAgentCore` — NOT `runProfile` (the narrowed one). Consider: the extension declares state for `cli` = on. The host passes `cliProfile`. Run-narrowing happens on capabilities, not extensions — an extension tool wires regardless of whether its host capability... wait, actually there's no gating of extensions against `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`! Interesting: the profile has a `hostExtensionApi` capability (all seven built-ins have it `on`). If a custom profile declares `hostExtensionApi` OFF, should extensions still wire? Let me check: `wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally. The plan gates the other capabilities but extensions are NOT gated on `plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability`. Hmm. Is that an issue?

Looking at the catalog: `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi: (all: {}, defaults: {})` — no required services. All seven built-in profiles declare it `on`. A custom profile could declare it `off` (e.g. "embed floor: no extension tools"). With this PR, the extension would STILL wire because `_wireExtensions` never consults the plan. # Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake

  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

The PR's own new test suite fails: 4 of the tests in `test/hosts/host_extension_api_test.dart` crash with `_TypeError: Null check operator used on a null value` at `host_agent_wiring.dart:740` (`_wireFabric`'s `services.hubFabric!`) before reaching their assertions. The author disclosed tests never ran locally ("static 1:1" verification; dart SIGKILLed) — and indeed they fail. Red CI guaranteed.
   - Root cause: the tests wire `cliProfile` with bare `AgentCoreServices` (no `sessionRoot`, no `hubFabric`). Run-narrowing drops `file`+`hub` transports but KEEPS `a2a` (the catalog declares no `requiredServicesByTransport` entry for `a2a`), producing a file-less, hub-less `CapabilityTransportState({a2a})`. `_wireFabric`'s file-less branch then assumes "the wired hub IS the fabric" and force-unwraps `services.hubFabric!` — the comment's invariant ("Null never rides here") is false for the a2a-only shape.
   - Fix options: (a) minimal — provide `sessionRoot` (+`hubFabric`/`mainMailbox`) in the bare services like `_subagentServices` does; or (b) builder-side — declare the a2a transport's service requirement and make `_wireFabric` treat a transport-only file-less shape as E1-loud instead of `!`.

**IMPORTANT:**
2. Extensions are not gated on the profile's `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi` plan state: `_wireExtensions` runs unconditionally in `wireAgentCore`, so a custom profile that declares `hostExtensionApi: off(reason)` still gets extension tools wired. All seven built-ins declare it `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged, but the matrix cell is currently decorative — the declared off cell has no effect, contradicting the builder's own "declare every host's cell" contract in AGENTS.md. (Worth either gating or an explicit follow-up note; slice 7 adds prompt sections/bridges but tools wire NOW.)

3. Latent builder bug exposed by the new tests (same root as #1): the a2a-only narrowed fabric shape crashes `_wireFabric`. Even after fixing the tests per (a), any real host that provides no sessionRoot/hubFabric (e.g. an a2a-centric embed) hits the same `hubFabric!` crash — an E1 violation of the builder's own "never null-crash" contract. - feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed

  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver

  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed

  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:

  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed

  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green

  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.

  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay

  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.

out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare

builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `tools` is stored raw while `profileStates` is defensively unmodifiable**

The constructor wraps the matrix with `Map.unmodifiable(profileStates)` but keeps `this.tools` as the caller's mutable list. The class is a `final class` with `final` fields — the declared shape reads immutable, but a host that mutates the list between construction and `wireAgentCore` silently changes what wires (the wire-time `List.unmodifiable(extension.tools)` copy protects the core, not the declaration the E7 reports and `WiredHostExtension.extension` expose).

```dart
HostExtension({
  required this.name,
  List<AgentTool> tools = const [],
  required Map<String, CapabilityState> profileStates,
}) : tools = List.unmodifiable(tools),
     profileStates = Map.unmodifiable(profileStates) {
```

(The existing duplicate-id loop then reads the unmodifiable copy — no behavior change.)

    feat(#1079): SDK slice 2 — live agent-stack wiring (wireAgentCore); CLI converts to the shared builder (#1230)
    
    * feat(#1079): SDK slice 2 — live agent-stack wiring through the builder; CLI is the first thin shell
    
    wireAgentCore (lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart, pure Dart): consumes a
    HostCapabilityProfile + typed AgentCoreServices and produces the wired core —
    run-narrowed plan, env chain (base → sandbox → session vars), the canonical
    capability-gated core tool list, and buildAgentStack (registry + Agent). Run
    narrowing turns wired capabilities with absent services into declared
    off(reason) states and drops unserved transports, so E1 stays loud for what
    remains wired; profiles still cannot force-enable past their floor.
    
    Catalog corrections (honest CLI evidence): messagingFabric hub and
    sqliteLspDap ffi/process services are per-transport (a host without one keeps
    the others); visionTranscribe requires nothing (per-tool config gating lives
    in the assembly — generate_image/generate_video register unconditionally).

registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.

  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake

  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /

  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
