(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

`dart test test/hosts` on this branch fails: **`+63 -4`**, and all four failures are in this new file. The author's local gate was never run (disclosed: dart SIGKILLed, "static 1:1" verification), and the tests do not hold.

Failing tests (all `_TypeError: Null check operator used on a null value` at `host_agent_wiring.dart:740`, `_wireFabric`):

1. E7 — "an extension id colliding with the SDK core…" (services built here, line 124) — expects `HostWiringException`, gets the null crash, so the E7 pin never asserts
2. E7 — "two extensions colliding with each other…" (line 146)
3. E8 — "a profile-off extension contributes no tools and surfaces its reason" (line 199) — crashes inside `wireAgentCore` before any expect
4. E8 — "an on extension wires its tools in the canonical tail position" (line 223)

**Root cause**: these four tests build `AgentCoreServices` with *bare* services — no `sessionRoot`, no `hubFabric`. For `cliProfile`, run-narrowing drops the `file` and `hub` messaging transports but **keeps `a2a`** (the catalog declares no `requiredServicesByTransport` entry for it), producing a file-less, hub-less `CapabilityTransportState({a2a})`. `_wireFabric`'s file-less branch then assumes "the wired hub IS the fabric" and force-unwraps `services.hubFabric!` → crash. This is a latent slice-2/3 builder hole that this PR's tests are the first to walk into (see the general comment for the builder-side half).

**Minimal fix (verified locally)**: give the four bare constructions a `sessionRoot` — exactly what the passing AC9 helper at line 279-285 and `_subagentServices` already do:

```dart
final services = AgentCoreServices(
  baseEnv: MemoryExecutionEnv(cwd: '/w'),
  sessionRoot: '/tmp/fah-test', // file transport wires → _wireFabric takes the normal path
  extensions: [ /* … */ ],
);
```

I reproduced both directions: the bare-services form crashes with the null check, and the same wiring with `sessionRoot` added passes. Alternatively (or additionally), fix the builder so an `a2a`-only narrowed fabric fails E1-loud instead of `!`-crashing — but as landed, CI's `test/hosts` stage will go red.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];

- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed

  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

(env chain + core tools + plan) and `buildAgentStack` (registry + agent)
out. The CLI (`AgentCli`) is the reference shell. Per-run narrowing:
a wired capability whose services the host did not provide turns
`off(reason)` for that run (a null config section is a declared state,
not a silent hand-rolled `if`), and wired transports with absent
per-transport services are dropped. When adding a capability: declare
every host's cell, add its `requiredServices` to the catalog, wire its
tools inside `wireAgentCore`'s canonical order, and extend the
hosts test — never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the
builder. The task/subagent complex (fabric → manager → heartbeat →
task/monitoring tools, slice 3) is builder-owned the same way: hosts pass
shell glue as `SubagentServices` callbacks and keep handles from
`WiredAgentCore` — a host never hand-assembles the manager or registers
`task` outside the gated surface. Host EXTENSIONS are declared surface
too (slice 4, `HostExtensionApi`, lib/src/hosts/host_extension_api.dart):
a `HostExtension` carries its tools plus an explicit state for every
built-in profile at birth (E6 — no implicit default; a custom profile
needs its state before wiring), the builder rejects tool-id collisions
across the core/task/extension surfaces at build time naming both
registrants (E7 — an extension id colliding with a core tool would
silently override SDK behavior, so the loud check lives in the builder,
not the child-lenient `ToolRegistry`), and an extension `off` on the
wired profile hides from the registry with its reason surfaced on
`WiredAgentCore.extensions` (E8). The extension surface is additive-only:
memory, context management, compaction, the JSONL tool session and
trajectory are SDK invariants with no override point (AC9).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. That capability exists precisely for this surface (catalog: *"Host extension API: registering host tools / prompt sections / bridges through the builder"*), and a custom profile can declare it `off(reason)` — but the declaration has zero effect: extension tools wire anyway.

All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart
final extensionsWired = plan.planFor(HostCapability.hostExtensionApi) is WiredCapability;
final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```

…or, if the gate is deliberately deferred to slice 7 (prompt sections/bridges), say so in the `HostExtension` dartdoc and AGENTS.md paragraph so hosts don't rely on the cell today. A test pinning the off-cell behavior belongs in `host_extension_api_test.dart` either way.

# Changelog

## 1.0.508


- feat(hosts): gh-1322 — the wireAgentCore host-adoption gaps: an embed
  guide (`docs/embedding.md`, with the explicit "hosts ride wireAgentCore,
  never adk_dart" rule), the host-facing key-slot resolver
  (`AgentCoreServices.resolveKey` + `HostKeyResolver` — the effective slot
  NAME, pinned-twin drift hints identical to the CLI's migration notes,
  registry-leg `knownSlotNames`, injected env/store readers only), and
  lifecycle telemetry for in-process hosts (`AgentCoreServices.telemetry`:
  the pure interface + in-memory ring in core, the fa.log file sink behind
  `lib/io.dart`; requestStart/firstToken/turn/tool/run records with
  durations and the provider HTTP status).
- chore(ci): document the sm-kicker head-completeness codeless-head crash
  (upstream awf#15) — the factory job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` before
  `--arg`/`--argjson`, so a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed
  files: a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff) crashes the
  job with `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4` — even when CI is fully green
  on that head, and the job's own rescue dispatch can never heal exactly
  those heads. Workaround until the upstream fix: keep the branch head
  code-bearing. Live instance: run 37193754301 on head 1fe9b1232.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 — `schedule_message` self-chains no longer die
  silently at the agent-chatter wake cap. The idle inbox-wake gate
  (`InboxWakePolicy`, shared by the CLI and the app hosts) now exempts a
  delivered scheduled self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to)
  from the 10-consecutive-wake streak: a deliberate agent-chosen cadence
  (night watch, periodic sweep) wakes forever, while foreign
  agent-to-agent chatter stays capped (anti-storm REG) and user-kind
  mail always wakes. A 30s cadence floor bounds a zero-delay
  re-schedule spin (E5). Refused wakes are visible (`[mail] wake
  refused`, once per episode) and every lifecycle step is receipted to
  `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`):
  scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed /
  wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused. A failed scheduler scan
  (transient `listDir` error) now re-arms at `failureBackoff` with an
  `onError` log instead of silently disarming the delivery heartbeat.
- fix(messaging): gh-1180 review round — refusal receipts and the
  visible refusal line are gated once per refusal EPISODE (the latch

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the `hostExtensionApi` capability cell is declared but never enforced**

`wireAgentCore` calls `_wireExtensions` unconditionally — nothing consults the run plan for `HostCapability.hostExtensionApi`. All seven built-in profiles declare the cell `on`, so built-in behavior is unchanged today. But the matrix contract being added to AGENTS.md in this same PR says *"When adding a capability: declare every host's cell … never gate tool registration with a bare `if` outside the builder"* — a custom embed host declaring `hostExtensionApi: off` (e.g. "no third-party tools in this embed") gets its extensions silently wired, contradicting the builder's own declare-to-wire invariant (E2: silence is not a declaration; the cell is decorative).

Either gate the extension resolution on the plan state, e.g.:

```dart

final extensionWiring = extensionsWired
    ? _wireExtensions(profileName: profile.name, extensions: services.extensions)
    : [for (final e in services.extensions) /* hidden with the cell's reason */];
```
